_doc: The seven universal player-behaviour presets. Game-independent: no game, mechanic, item or node path appears here.
Every trait is normalized to 0..1 (0 = none/lowest, 1 = strongest). Habits (attention, sessions) and goals (exploration,
collection, completion, urgency) are separate axes and can be overridden independently per run without changing a preset.
The session patterns are editable defaults for simulation, NOT measured human population statistics.
Derived engine values (decision interval, commitment hold, confidence gate...) are computed from the traits by
core/profile_library.gd; the formulas are documented there and in README.md.

attention.meaning: how often the player makes deliberate decisions and how quickly urgent situations are noticed

efficiency.meaning: how sharply the player distinguishes better from worse options (optimization)

main_goal_urgency.meaning: pressure to advance the main objective/milestones

risk_tolerance.meaning: willingness to accept options that can fail or lose progress

spending.meaning: spends resources now vs saves for a chosen goal
spending.high: buys whatever is useful and affordable

preparation.meaning: how prepared the player wants to be before a risky attempt

collection_drive.meaning: drive to own new/unowned/rare items and variety

completion_drive.meaning: drive to finish accessible goals before advancing

automation_preference.meaning: preference for passive, offline and automation systems when the game offers them

setback_tolerance.meaning: how readily the player retries after a failure
setback_tolerance.low: backs off for long and grows cautious

revisit_tendency.meaning: how readily the player revisits a committed plan

mastery.low: new to the genre, avoids unfamiliar features

learning_rate.meaning: how fast familiarity grows and mistakes fade with experience

mistake_rate.meaning: initial chance of a bounded, explainable mistake (choosing a plausible runner-up)

active.summary: Plays often and for long stretches, decides frequently, explores and pursues progression, learns and uses the tools available.
active.constraint: Engaged is not optimal or omniscient; avoids permanent hoarding and aimless grinding.

casual.summary: Short, intermittent sessions; moderate decisions; follows understandable goals; explores occasionally; spends when the benefit is clear.
casual.constraint: Less optimized than Active; interruptions and missed opportunities are plausible, not artificial penalties.

idle.summary: Very brief, infrequent interaction; prioritizes passive and automation systems if the game offers them; few manual decisions.
idle.constraint: Without offline or automation systems this is low attention only; it never invents passive rewards.

beginner.summary: New to the game's systems: tentative exploration, slower and less consistent decisions, some understandable mistakes, cautious with unfamiliar features.
beginner.constraint: Imperfection is bounded and explainable (plausible runner-up choices, avoidance of unfamiliar features) and fades as it learns; never sabotage.

collector.summary: Seeks items, discoveries, variety, sets and rare or unowned content; willing to delay the main progression for collection.
collector.constraint: Collection first is not 100% completion of every mission or upgrade.

speedrunner.summary: Reaches explicit milestones as quickly as it can: skips optional tasks, accepts calculated risk, spends only to remove progression bottlenecks.
speedrunner.constraint: Fast is not omniscient, instant or a cheat; failures and resets cost real simulated time.

completionist.summary: Finishes accessible goals, upgrades, achievements and optional objectives before advancing; methodical and persistent.
completionist.constraint: Broader than Collector; respects accessibility and gives up on unreachable targets instead of looping forever.
